figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Overall strategy and results of this study. The putative AN6791 biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC), located on chromosome I, harbors two
putative Zn(II)2Cys6 transcription factor genes (AN6788 and AN6790). We fused the native DNA binding domain (DBD) of AN6788 with the
AfoA activation domain (AD) to create a hybrid transcription factor. We created a strain in which both the hybrid AN6788-AfoA transcription
factor and AN6790 are under control of the inducible promoter alcA(p). Metabolic profiling of this strain after induction of AN6788-AfoA and
AN6790 expression revealed the production of 1, 2, and 3. Targeted gene deletions revealed these compounds do not require the highly reducing
polyketide synthase AN6791 for their production. Rather, they are synthesized via the nonreducing polyketide synthase AN3230 (pkfA) encoded
within the pkf biosynthetic gene cluster located on chromosome VI.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Strategy to generate a strain of A. nidulans that expresses a hybrid AN6788 transcription factor to promote polyketide biosynthesis. We
constructed, by fusion PCR, a fragment consisting of a yA 5′ flanking sequence, the selectable marker AtpyrG, and alcA(p) fused to the DNA
binding domain (DBD) of AN6788 and a portion of the afoA activation domain (AD). Transformation of this construct into strain LO9577
resulted in homologous recombination at the yA locus creating a hybrid transcription factor gene under control of alcA(p) and encoding the
AN6788 DNA binding domain, the AfoA activation domain and the remainder of AfoA. The resulting strains, LO10141 and 10145, are capable of
inducible expression of the hybrid AN6788 transcription factor.
